source: WriteStallTimeoutHandler on a CONNECT tunnel's client connection (the loopback leg is exempt) closes it when its client took none of the tunnelled response for responseWriteStallTimeoutMillis, and counts it in mock_server_response_write_stalls_total{protocol=tunnel,scope=connection}, the relay being asked for first (MetricsTest#countsResponseWriteStallsUnderTheirProtocolAndScope). maxRequestBodySize is raised because the oracle's relay aggregates the loopback's response under it and a 30 MB one would fail (TooLongHttpContentException, a 502). logLevel WARN keeps the tens of MB out of the event log, whose rendering starved the timed scenarios replayed in the same process

steps.note: a 30 MB response through a CONNECT tunnel whose client stops reading: cut after a second, before it is all sent

mask.reason: only the series this scenario drives; the rest are pinned by metrics.json

steps.note: the WARN, with the bytes waiting for the client when it was cut

mask.reason: the 30 MB response, logged when it was returned

Netty's ChannelOutboundBuffer.totalPendingWriteBytes (the unwritten messages plus 96 bytes of entry overhead each: 32864 for one 32 KiB slice of PacedLargeWriteHandler, 30000096 for a 30 MB binary answer written whole) against the rest of the write our socket has not taken, which depends on socket buffers
